# Per-position IOI SAE analysis: final report

*Generated by `src/run_position_pipeline.py` from `results_positional_300/positional_activations.npy` (GPT-2 small, `gpt2-small-res-jb`, `blocks.8.hook_resid_pre`). Every number below is computed from the step outputs in this folder.*

## 1. Data and verification

300 prompts, 61 failures, 239 successes (accuracy 0.797); tensor shape (300, 3, 24576) (example, window position, SAE feature). Direction everywhere: **failure minus success**. Verification (`verify_positional_data.py`): all checks passed (labels equal the original `predictions.csv`; token indices are the true tail of each prompt; the 3-position mean reproduces the original `activations.npy`).

## 2. What the positions are

* **Position 1** (offset -3): ` the` 54/187 fail, ` a` 7/113 fail
* **Position 2** (offset -2): ` keys` 42/45 fail, ` card` 0/43 fail, ` flowers` 4/39 fail, ` book` 5/37 fail, ` gift` 6/37 fail, ` bag` 0/36 fail, ` drink` 2/33 fail, ` ball` 2/30 fail
* **Position 3** (offset -1): ` to` 61/300 fail

Positions are counted from the end of the prompt, not semantic slots. Object identity determines the tokens at positions 1 and 2.

## 3. Which features differ between failures and successes

| position | tested | Welch+Holm<.05 (higher in failure) | max-T<.05 | stratified by object | stratified by template | |d|>0.8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 293 | 24 (3) | 24 | 0 | 26 | 0 |
| 2 | 426 | 70 (39) | 72 | 0 | 79 | 57 |
| 3 | 412 | 76 (30) | 84 | 0 | 93 | 79 |

Holm is over the complete 3 x 24,576 family. Welch p-values are anti-conservative for sparse features, so the max-T permutation column is the more reliable one. 'Stratified' = labels shuffled only within each object (or template) and activations centred within it: association beyond that variable.

## 5. Template, object and article effects

* Template, all prompts: permutation p = 0.534.
* Keys prompts only: 42/45 fail, template p = 0.245.
* Non-keys prompts only: 19/255 fail; template p = 0.0010; failures by template {'0': 1, '1': 1, '2': 4, '3': 13}.
* Template 3: 13/77 fail vs 6/178 elsewhere (Fisher p = 0.0004); text: `Once Susan and Dan arrived at the park, Susan passed the keys to`.
* Details and failure modes: `template_analysis.md`. These tests are post hoc and unadjusted across each other.

## 6. Stability

| position | top-20 mean bootstrap recurrence | split-half held-out d (real / label-permuted) | same-sign fraction (real / permuted) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.65 | +0.27 / +0.01 | 0.83 / 0.43 |
| 2 | 0.90 | +2.19 / +0.00 | 1.00 / 0.40 |
| 3 | 0.93 | +2.46 / +0.00 | 1.00 / 0.41 |

Top-5 failure-side features per position, smallest d within any single template: position 1: +0.27, position 2: +1.56, position 3: +1.58; smallest d when any one template is left out: position 1: +0.38, position 2: +2.09, position 3: +2.29.

Stability here means the finding is reproducible within this 300-prompt sample (and across templates, see `stability.md`); it does not mean it is causal or independent of the object confound. A fresh-seed corpus needs the model (`build_task_set.py --seed`, then the positional runner).

## 7. Conclusions supported by these outputs

* Unstratified, 79 failure-higher features at positions 2-3 pass max-T; the strongest are active almost exactly on the keys prompts (table in section 3).
* Stratified by object: 0 features (any position) remain significant -- no evidence of association beyond object identity in this sample.
* Stratified by template (labels shuffled within template): 198 features significant overall; 10 of the 10 strongest position-2/3 failure features remain significant, so these are not a template artifact.

## 8. Limitations

* Only 19 failures outside keys and 3 successes inside keys: the stratified tests have low power; 'not significant' is not 'absent'.
* One model, SAE, layer and task; 300 prompts from one generator; associations only, no causal claim (ablations are not re-run here).
* Last-3 positions are end-relative; token identity is part of what is measured.
